sampling_model.design: For each \(\rho\in I\), the chronological two-stage adaptive enrichment law \(\mathsf P_n^{h,\rho}\) fixes \(B_n\), forms \(Y^{(h)}(0)=B\) and \(Y^{(h)}(1)=B+h_s/\sqrt n\), draws independent stratumwise simple-random holdouts of the \(\rho\)-specified sizes, completely randomizes stage 1, realizes the complete signed recruitment cell, and only then completely randomizes stage 2 within recruited strata conditional on the history. The resulting dataset is \(\mathcal D_n^{h,\rho}\). Its Fisher reference uses the same \(\rho\), enumerates the exact candidate support \(\Omega_{n,1s}(\rho)\), recomputes the selector and complete cell under the sharp-zero completion, retains exactly the observed cell, and then enumerates stage-2 assignments only in retained strata. Its cell probability, kernel, cdf, critical value, and reference distance are all indexed by that design value and realized dataset.
sampling_model.units: A fixed baseline finite-population triangular array in two strata and two stages; under \(\mathsf P_n^{h,\rho}\), the only randomness is the holdout and chronological treatment assignment.
sampling_model.treatment: Balanced binary treatment is completely randomized in every stage-1 stratum and, after recruitment, in each selected stage-2 stratum under its history-conditional kernel.
sampling_model.overlap: Both treatment arms have positive limiting shares, every complete signed cell represented in the active index set has probability at least \(\epsilon\), and the limiting selected Gaussian residual variance satisfies \(v_j(\rho,\theta_j)^2\ge\rho\ge\rho_0\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The exact complement Neyman studentizer, normalized-midrank permutation studentizers, random complement counts, pair-spacing slopes, and mean--rank correlations are embedded jointly in the finite-population transfer. Maximum-influence ratios are derived from the empirical centered fourth-moment bound, finite-population variance margin, and positive shares; no oracle nuisance quantity or separate Lindeberg premise is assumed.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Proposition 1 gives superuniform selective validity and type-I control, while Proposition 2 gives the conditional reference representation and computability under imputability.
Theorems 2 and 4 give multivariate Gaussian limits for random partitions and general completely randomized finite-population estimators.
Theorem 1 bounds Gaussian approximation error for linear permutation contrasts under complete randomization.
Theorem 9 transfers weak convergence through randomized selection under independent sampling.
Theorems 1.1 and 2.2 establish Ehrhard--Borell Gaussian convexity and classify equality.
Theorem 1 represents sequential enrichment policies by trajectory variables and validates the sparse optimization formulation.
Theorem 3.7 identifies the extra leftover-information statistic for location-invariant Gaussian adaptive experiments.

body.tldr: For a two-stratum, two-stage enrichment experiment, fix a baseline array \(B_n\) and generate local alternatives by \(Y^{(h)}(0)=B\) and \(Y^{(h)}(1)=B+h_s/\sqrt n\). Each holdout value \(\rho\) defines its own chronological sampling law \(\mathsf P_n^{h,\rho}\), realized dataset \(\mathcal D_n^{h,\rho}\), and same-design Fisher sharp-null reference. The reference enumerates all quota-respecting holdout--assignment pairs, recomputes the selector from completed outcomes, retains exactly the observed complete signed cell, then randomizes stage 2 only in retained strata; its support and cell probability are explicit. For every admissible baseline array, an array-dependent remainder separately transfers the sampling cdf to the shifted Gaussian law and the indexed random reference cdf to its zero-drift law. The finite-population maximum-influence ratios are derived from the empirical centered fourth-moment bound, variance margin, and positive shares, while the limiting Gaussian residual variance is bounded below by \(\rho_0\) from the holdout design itself. Cross-stratum factorization reduces both limits to scalar critical-value and power integrals. Selected-score quantiles are convex, with chord equality exactly when the correlation is zero or the chord endpoints coincide, and reduce every compact positive alternative set to its least coordinate. The sign of \(\Delta_j=A_s-\kappa_jb_{1j}\) determines the weight side; nonnegative discrepancies force the largest holdout, an explicit two-component uniform mixture verifies both sampling and random-reference margins and yields a certified interior regime, and mixed signs admit an equality-aware analytic optimizer correspondence with tolerance-certified boxes.

project_justification.gap: Freidling, Zhao, and Gao establish exact selective randomization inference and explicitly leave holdout allocation and powerful selection-dependent statistics open. Existing finite-population central limit theorems are unconditional, selective central limit theorems use independent sampling with smooth external randomization, and enrichment-design optimization uses model-based numerical programs. None supplies a design-uniform, array-specific without-replacement transfer that separates the shifted sampling law from the dataset-dependent Fisher reference, or an analytic holdout--weight power frontier.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is a design-based maximin conditional-local-power problem in which the holdout fraction changes both the selection law and the amount of stage-1 randomization information retained for exact testing. Its optimizer may be an endpoint, an interior point, or a set-valued mixed-sign correspondence, so neither heuristic weight choice nor a floating-point optimizer resolves the design question.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the complete signed-cell selected Gaussian limit from a fixed baseline array and the separately indexed local-alternative laws \(\{\mathsf P_n^{h,\rho}:\rho\in I,h\in H\}\). For each \(\rho\), it constructs from \(\mathcal D_n^{h,\rho}\) the same-design Fisher completion and the exact finite support of quota-respecting candidate histories, recomputes selection for every candidate, retains exactly the observed complete cell, and integrates the ensuing stage-2 kernels. The reference cell probability is an explicit combinatorial sum. A deterministic sampling-cell margin is separated from a random-reference margin stated uniformly in probability. For each admissible baseline array, one common array-dependent modulus controls the sampling-cdf family uniformly over design and alternatives and controls the reference family through an outer supremum of the corresponding sampling probabilities. The required finite-population maximum-influence ratios follow from explicit inequalities using \(M_4\), \(\epsilon\), and positive block shares, and the limiting Gaussian residual variance obeys \(v_j^2\ge\rho\ge\rho_0\); neither is imposed separately. Cross-stratum factorization then yields the scalar selected integrals, which are solved through selected-quantile convexity with the exact chord-equality predicate, inverse-Mills factorization, realizability inequalities, analytic branch exhaustion, and certificate-aware interval computation. The newly maintained pair-spacing condition is realized directly by bounded continuous-density quantile arrays. The negative-discrepancy regime is anchored by deterministic quantiles from an explicit two-component uniform mixture with stated weights, supports, stratum allocations, exact primitive limits, reference-margin convergence, and certified enclosures.

body.related_work: Freidling, Zhao, and Gao's Proposition 1 gives superuniform selective validity and type-I control, Proposition 2 gives the conditional reference representation and its computability under imputability, and Section 5 motivates holdout and statistic design in two-stage enrichment. The exact candidate-history support here specializes that representation by enumerating every quota-respecting holdout--assignment pair, recomputing the complete cell, and integrating only the stage-2 kernels for retained strata. The asymptotic statement separately transfers the shifted sampling cdf under \(\mathsf P_n^{h,\rho}\) and the data-dependent Fisher-reference cdf under \(\mathsf R_{n,\mathcal D(\rho)}^{0,C}\), with distinct sampling and random-reference margins. Li and Ding provide the vector finite-population central limit theorem used to embed assignment contrasts, and Shi and Ding provide quantitative permutation-approximation and variance-estimation ingredients. In the present class, their maximum-influence premise is verified by explicit centered-outcome and normalized-midrank bounds rather than separately assumed. Tian and Taylor supply the conditional likelihood-transfer architecture in an iid randomized-selection model; the needed limiting residual-scale bound here instead follows algebraically from \(\rho\ge\rho_0\) and \(\lvert\kappa_j\rvert\le1\). Shenfeld and van Handel supply the Ehrhard--Borell machinery from which selected-quantile convexity and its chord-equality classification are derived. Rosenblum, Fang, and Liu provide the nearest two-stage enrichment optimization benchmark, but their sparse program targets model-based operating characteristics rather than exact full-cell conditional-randomization local power. Chen and Andrews characterize optimal conditional inference in parametric Gaussian adaptive experiments; the present design problem instead uses fixed baseline populations and without-replacement assignment. Thall's review confirms that subgroup selection, trial utility, and inferential quality remain distinct design axes.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The central proof risk is the per-array common transfer in \(\mathrm{thm{:}uniform\mbox{-}selected\mbox{-}transfer}\). For every design value \(\rho\), the true experiment fixes \(B_n\), uses \(Y^{(h)}(0)=B\) and \(Y^{(h)}(1)=B+h_s/\sqrt n\), and samples under its separately indexed law \(\mathsf P_n^{h,\rho}\); it never treats a positive local alternative as satisfying the sharp null. Each \(\rho\)-indexed dataset induces its own Fisher completion and explicit same-cell candidate-history support \(\Omega_{n,C}(\mathcal D_n^{h,\rho},\rho)\), with no further imputability event. Uniformity in \(\rho\) is asserted only through outer probabilities under the corresponding laws. The sampling-cell margin is deterministic, whereas the reference-cell margin is convergence in probability of the random combinatorial probability \(p_{\mathrm{ref}}\). The scalar formulas are licensed only after cross-stratum factorization under the sampling, explicit reference, and Gaussian laws. The maximum-influence step is settled by \(\mathrm{lem{:}derived\mbox{-}max\mbox{-}influence}\): the centered baseline ratio is at most \(\sqrt{M_4N_{nks}}/((N_{nks}-1)\epsilon)\), and the centered-midrank ratio is at most \(1/((N_{nks}-1)\epsilon)\). The Gaussian residual variance is at least \(\rho_0\) by \(\mathrm{lem{:}derived\mbox{-}residual\mbox{-}scale}\), but that limiting identity is not used as a finite-\(n\) covariance bound. The remaining proof must control hypergeometric complement counts, both studentizers, local rank drift under the newly maintained pair-spacing condition, null imputation, conditional cdfs, and moving quantiles with \(\eta_n(B)\), uniformly over \(\rho\), \(\theta\), and \(h\) for each fixed admissible baseline array, using \(\min\{\epsilon,\rho_0\}\) when a common variance, selection, and residual-scale margin is required. No deterministic rate uniform over the qualitative class \(\mathcal M\) is claimed. The early kill test is the two-law transfer and reference-margin verification for the explicit bounded nonproportional mixture family.
body.honest_scope: Finite-sample exactness is asserted only at the prespecified Fisher sharp-zero null \(h=0\). Positive local alternatives are sampled from \(Y^{(h)}\) under the separately indexed law \(\mathsf P_n^{h,\rho}\); for every \(\rho\), the realized dataset defines a separate same-design completion and an explicit candidate-history support obtained by recomputing the selector and retaining exactly the observed complete cell. No unspecified imputability fiber is conditioned upon. Uniform-in-\(\rho\) reference transfer means an outer supremum of the corresponding \(\mathsf P_n^{h,\rho}\)-probabilities. The sampling-cell margin is deterministic; the random reference-cell margin is a separate convergence-in-probability condition, verified for \(W_{\mathrm{mix}}\). The sampling cdf converges to a shifted selected Gaussian law, whereas each data-dependent reference cdf converges in its corresponding sampling probability to the zero-drift law. For each admissible \(B\), the same array-dependent \(\eta_n(B)\) is uniform over holdouts, weights, and compact local alternatives, but no rate is uniform over all of \(\mathcal M\). Maximum influence is derived from the empirical centered fourth-moment bound, the finite-population variance margin, and positive shares. The bound \(v_j^2\ge\rho_0\) concerns the limiting Gaussian residual only and supplies no finite-\(n\) covariance assertion. Whenever the proof needs one common lower constant across maintained finite-population margins and this limiting residual bound, it uses \(\min\{\epsilon,\rho_0\}\). The scalar formulas apply only to active \(j=(C,s)\) with \(C_s=1\) after complete-cell product cancellation. The pair-spacing condition is a newly maintained primitive condition realized by bounded continuous-density quantile arrays. The selected-quantile chord equality is exactly \(\operatorname{Eq}_{\beta,r}(c_0,c_1;t)\), classified by \(r=0\) or \(c_0=c_1\). The mixture certificate separates both holdout endpoints without asserting a unique interior optimizer; general computation remains set-valued unless a separation certificate proves uniqueness. Binary outcomes, nonzero sharp-null inversion, weak average-effect nulls, deterministic outcome-dependent splits, and continuous-biomarker cutoffs remain outside scope.
